title: Compactifications of morphisms over a qcqs base
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $X$ be an $S$-scheme that is separated
and of finite type over $S$, and let $Y$ be an $S$-scheme that is separated and quasi-compact
over $S$. Then every $S$-morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ has a compactification
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]).

proof.text: Write $a_X\colon X\to S$ and $a_Y\colon Y\to S$ for the structure morphisms. Because $f$ is an $S$-morphism, $a_X=a_Y\circ f$ by [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $a_X$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. The separated morphism $a_Y$ is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to $a_X$ and the quasi-compact scheme $S$ to obtain that $X$ is quasi-compact. Apply the same clause to $a_Y$: its quasi-compactness and the quasi-compactness of $S$ give quasi-compactness of $Y$; its quasi-separatedness and the quasi-separatedness of $S$ give quasi-separatedness of $Y$.

source.place: ## Proof: structure maps, quasi-compact source and qcqs target

proof.text: Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] to $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{a_Y}S$. Its composite is $a_X$, which is separated, so $f$ is separated. Apply clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to this triangle: since $a_X$ is locally of finite type, $f$ is locally of finite type. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] applies because Step 1 gives $X$ quasi-compact and $Y$ quasi-separated; hence $f$ is quasi-compact. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the last two assertions mean precisely that $f$ is of finite type.

source.place: ## Proof: separatedness, local finite type, and quasi-compactness of f

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] to $f\colon X\to Y$, with the theorem's base scheme equal to $Y$. Step 1 supplies the quasi-compact and quasi-separated base; Step 2 supplies the separated finite-type morphism. The theorem gives a dense compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$. By [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], $p\circ j=f$, $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ is proper. Forgetting the additional scheme-theoretic density condition gives the required compactification.

source.place: ## Proof, final sentence: apply Nagata compactification over Y
